title: AQ Podcast | Venezuela's Transition Talks
gist: A new round of Venezuela transition talks pairs opposition figure Dinorah Figuera with Jorge Rodríguez, brother of acting president Delcy Rodríguez, coming over seven months after the U.S. captured Nicolás Maduro and giving Washington unprecedented leverage over Venezuelan affairs.

insights.claim: Venezuela's chavista regime and parts of the political opposition are holding a new round of transition talks that analysts and citizens hope could lead to a democratic transition.
insights.speaker: Americas Quarterly
insights.so_what: A live regime-opposition dialogue is a headline catalyst for any Venezuela sanctions, oil-sector, or political-risk thesis — watch for concrete outcomes versus stalling.
insights.locator: Venezuela's regime and parts of the political opposition

insights.claim: The talks pair Dinorah Figuera, representing the opposition-aligned 2015 National Assembly, with Jorge Rodríguez, brother of acting president Delcy Rodríguez and current head of the legislature.
insights.speaker: Americas Quarterly
insights.so_what: Identifies the actual negotiating parties — track statements from Figuera and Jorge Rodríguez as the clearest signal of talks' direction.
insights.locator: The dialogue brings together Dinorah Figuera

insights.claim: The talks come more than seven months after the U.S. captured Nicolás Maduro on January 3rd, at a moment when Washington has unprecedented leverage over Venezuelan affairs.
insights.speaker: Americas Quarterly
insights.so_what: Confirms Maduro is no longer in power and under U.S. custody, and frames current negotiations as happening under maximal U.S. bargaining leverage — a key input for any Venezuela oil-sanctions-relief timeline.
insights.quote: more than seven months after the U.S. capture of Nicolás Maduro on January 3rd
insights.locator: It comes more than seven months after

insights.claim: María Corina Machado, a prominent opposition leader, is notably absent from the transition talks, raising questions about what role she will play in the process.
insights.speaker: Americas Quarterly
insights.so_what: Machado's exclusion or non-participation is a risk flag for the legitimacy and durability of any deal reached without her buy-in.
insights.locator: what role María Corina Machado will play

insights.claim: The central open question framed by the podcast is whether the chavista regime under Delcy Rodríguez is pursuing genuine political change or simply stalling for time until Trump leaves office.
insights.speaker: Americas Quarterly
insights.so_what: Frames the key variable for Venezuela risk pricing: a stalling regime implies prolonged sanctions/political uncertainty versus a genuine-transition scenario that could open oil-sector and debt-restructuring upside.
insights.locator: whether the chavista regime is pursuing genuine change
